The US-China trade truce was not extended during weekend talks despite optimistic rhetoric, and it expires November 10th, leaving a live uncertainty overhang. AMD is among the top outperformers Monday on the thesis that agentic AI — which Meta Muse could bring to the mainstream — is significantly more CPU-intensive than prior AI iterations, directly benefiting CPU-linked chipmakers. The Meta Muse demand narrative is acting as a sector-wide re-rating event for CPU exposure.

Intel is rallying alongside AMD on the agentic AI CPU demand thesis, with the market pricing in that a mainstream consumer AI agent wave would meaningfully increase compute demand for CPU-intensive workloads. Intel is one of the named outperformers in today's tech surge.

HP Inc. is sliding after the company indicated it anticipates PC unit volumes will fall approximately 5% in calendar year 2027, providing a cautious demand outlook for the PC market. This is weighing on the broader PC supply chain even as AI hardware names surge.

Reports indicate Paramount may agree to preserve CNN's editorial independence and divest certain cable channels including Comedy Central as part of the settlement.

The company did tout future blockbuster launches but lacked the specificity the market wanted.

Disney's parks business is outperforming industry peers, many of whom are experiencing traffic headwinds, by leaning on price promotions and package deals to drive attendance. The Wall Street Journal highlighted the strategy as differentiating Disney from the broader theme park industry slump.

Oracle was the subject of a negative Financial Times article Friday, focusing on poor price action in debt tied to its massive data center project in New Mexico known as Project Jupiter. Efforts to offload loans tied to the facility have reportedly hit a wall, raising questions about execution on its aggressive infrastructure buildout.

CF Industries and other potash-linked names — Mosaic and Nutrien — all slumped after Trump said the US was nearing a massive supply deal with Belarus with pricing substantially below what is currently being paid for Canadian potash. The news is a direct pricing headwind for North American potash producers.

tts_summary:
Here's your midday update for Monday, September 21st. Two big stories are driving today's session and they are pulling markets in very different directions depending on where you sit.

First, the macro setup. Stocks are broadly higher but the gains are very concentrated. The Nasdaq is up 153 basis points, the S&P 500 is up 94 basis points, but the equal-weight S&P is barely up 30 basis points. That's a narrow, top-heavy rally. Treasuries have a modest bid, yields down one to three basis points across the curve. Brent crude is getting hit hard, down roughly 400 basis points and trading below a hundred dollars a barrel.

Now the two themes. Theme one is Meta Muse. Reports of strong consumer demand for the app and anticipation of Zuckerberg's keynote at the Connect Conference Wednesday night are lighting up the entire AI complex. The key insight here is that agentic AI — which Muse could help push into the mainstream — is far more CPU-intensive than prior AI iterations. That makes it directly bullish for Advanced Micro Devices, ARM, and Intel, all of which are among today's top performers. OpenAI is reportedly scrambling to develop a competing product. This is a genuine product cycle signal, not just hype.

Theme two is oil and geopolitics. Trump called off planned airstrikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night, and markets are pricing in diplomatic optimism ahead of this week's United Nations General Assembly in New York. Trump could potentially meet with Iran's president. That's sending energy stocks lower — names like Exxon, ConocoPhillips, Devon, and Pioneer are all in the red.

On the company side, Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery are both jumping after Paramount struck a deal with state attorneys general to settle the lawsuit blocking their merger, clearing a major regulatory hurdle. HP Inc. is sliding after guiding to a roughly five percent decline in PC unit volumes in calendar 2027 — a cautious read on consumer hardware demand. Novo Nordisk disappointed at its analyst day in Europe, failing to provide granular enough financial targets despite touting future pipeline launches. And Oracle is facing scrutiny after a negative report on poor price action in debt tied to its New Mexico data center project, with loan offloading efforts reportedly hitting a wall. Potash names — CF Industries, Mosaic, and Nutrien — are all getting crushed after Trump said the US is nearing a massive fertilizer supply deal with Belarus at prices substantially below Canadian potash.

The bear case today is straightforward — this rally is thin, geopolitical risk has been deferred not resolved, the US-China trade truce still has no extension with a November 10th expiration looming, and the AI infrastructure spending wave is burning cash at a staggering rate with OpenAI projecting negative free cash flow of roughly 280 billion dollars over the next four years.

The bull case is the Meta Muse catalyst is real, oil dropping below a hundred is a genuine macro tailwind, and diplomatic progress at the UN could extend the relief rally into the back half of the week. Watch Zuckerberg Wednesday night — that's the next major signpost.
